Hold on to your tails!'},\n {key: 'chaos_finale_2', text: 'Everything is happening at once!'}\n ]\n }\n }\n};\n","/**\n * Outfit rolling for Squirrel Scramble (SPEC.md § 9). Outfits are cosmetic: rolled in the browser\n * from a seeded generator, stored with the entrant at draw time, and drawn again on replay.\n *\n * Each slot (hat, cape, accessory, fur) rolls a rarity first (common 80, rare 17, legendary 3)\n * and then picks uniformly among that slot's items of that rarity. The catalogue lives in the\n * theme config, so a new hat is a data entry and an SVG fragment, never a server change.\n *\n * Pure ES module: no DOM, no Lit and no platform imports.\n */\nimport {themeConfig} from './theme-config.js';\n\n// The server accepts exactly these keys (SPEC.md § 7, outfit validation).\nconst PAYLOAD_SLOTS = ['hat', 'cape', 'accessory', 'fur'];\n\n/** Every outfit id the server accepts (SPEC.md § 7). */\nexport const OUTFIT_ID_PATTERN = /^[a-z0-9_]{1,24}$/;\n\n/**\n * @description Rolls one rarity by the catalogue's weights.\n * @param {{nextFloat: function(): number, weightedIndex: function(number[]): number}} rng -\n * A seeded generator from createRng().\n * @param {Object} catalogue - The theme's outfits section.\n * @returns {string} A rarity name.\n * @since 1.0.0\n */\nfunction rollRarity(rng, catalogue) {\n const weights = catalogue.rarityOrder.map((rarity) => catalogue.rarityWeights[rarity] || 0);\n return catalogue.rarityOrder[rng.weightedIndex(weights)];\n}\n\n/**\n * @description Returns a slot's items of the given rarity. A slot with no item of that rarity\n * falls back to the next more common tier, so a short catalogue still rolls.\n * @param {Array<{id: string, rarity: string}>} slotItems - The slot's catalogue entries.\n * @param {string} rarity - The rolled rarity.\n * @param {string[]} rarityOrder - Rarities from most to least common.\n * @returns {Array<{id: string, rarity: string}>} The candidates (never empty for a non-empty\n * slot).\n * @since 1.0.0\n */\nfunction itemsOfRarity(slotItems, rarity, rarityOrder) {\n for (let rank = rarityOrder.indexOf(rarity); rank >= 0; rank -= 1) {\n const matches = slotItems.filter((item) => item.rarity === rarityOrder[rank]);\n if (matches.length > 0) {\n return matches;\n }\n }\n return slotItems;\n}\n\n/**\n * @description Finds a catalogue entry by slot and id.\n * @param {string} slot - The slot name.\n * @param {*} id - The item id.\n * @param {Object} catalogue - The theme's outfits section.\n * @returns {{id: string, label: string, rarity: string}|null} The entry, or null.\n * @since 1.0.0\n */\nfunction findItem(slot, id, catalogue) {\n const items = catalogue.slots[slot] || [];\n return items.find((item) => item.id === id) || null;\n}\n\n/**\n * @description Rolls a whole outfit: one item per slot, in the catalogue's slot order. Uses two\n * generator draws per slot (rarity, then item), always in that order.\n * @param {Object} rng - A seeded generator from createRng().\n * @param {Object} [catalogue] - The theme's outfits section.\n * @returns {{hat: string, cape: string, accessory: string, fur: string}} Item ids.\n * @example\n * const outfit = rollOutfit(createRng(randomSeed()));\n * @since 1.0.0\n */\nexport function rollOutfit(rng, catalogue = themeConfig.outfits) {\n const outfit = {};\n catalogue.slotOrder.forEach((slot) => {\n const rarity = rollRarity(rng, catalogue);\n const candidates = itemsOfRarity(catalogue.slots[slot], rarity, catalogue.rarityOrder);\n outfit[slot] = rng.pick(candidates).id;\n });\n return outfit;\n}\n\n/**\n * @description Rolls one outfit per squirrel.\n * @param {Object} rng - A seeded generator from createRng().\n * @param {number} count - How many outfits.\n * @param {Object} [catalogue] - The theme's outfits section.\n * @returns {Array<Object>} The outfits.\n * @example\n * const outfits = rollOutfits(rng, names.length);\n * @since 1.0.0\n */\nexport function rollOutfits(rng, count, catalogue = themeConfig.outfits) {\n return Array.from({length: Math.max(0, count)}, () => rollOutfit(rng, catalogue));\n}\n\n/**\n * @description Re-rolls every outfit except the padlocked ones (\"Shuffle outfits\"). Returns a new\n * array; the input array and its outfits are untouched.\n * @param {Object} rng - A seeded generator from createRng().\n * @param {Array<Object>} outfits - The current outfits, one per squirrel.\n * @param {Iterable<number>} [lockedIndexes] - Indexes to keep.\n * @param {Object} [catalogue] - The theme's outfits section.\n * @returns {Array<Object>} The new outfits.\n * @example\n * const next = rerollOutfits(rng, outfits, [0, 3]);\n * @since 1.0.0\n */\nexport function rerollOutfits(rng, outfits, lockedIndexes = [], catalogue = themeConfig.outfits) {\n const locked = new Set(lockedIndexes);\n return outfits.map((outfit, index) => (\n locked.has(index) ? {...outfit} : rollOutfit(rng, catalogue)\n ));\n}\n\n/**\n * @description Returns the rarity of one item. Unknown ids count as the most common rarity.\n * @param {string} slot - The slot name.\n * @param {string} id - The item id.\n * @param {Object} [catalogue] - The theme's outfits section.\n * @returns {string} The rarity name.\n * @example\n * itemRarity('hat', 'crown');\n * // 'legendary'\n * @since 1.0.0\n */\nexport function itemRarity(slot, id, catalogue = themeConfig.outfits) {\n const item = findItem(slot, id, catalogue);\n return item ? item.rarity : catalogue.rarityOrder[0];\n}\n\n/**\n * @description Returns the rarest tier of any item in an outfit.\n * @param {Object} outfit - An outfit (missing slots and unknown ids count as common).\n * @param {Object} [catalogue] - The theme's outfits section.\n * @returns {string} The rarity name.\n * @example\n * outfitRarity({hat: 'halo', fur: 'red'});\n * // 'rare'\n * @since 1.0.0\n */\nexport function outfitRarity(outfit, catalogue = themeConfig.outfits) {\n const source = outfit && typeof outfit === 'object' ? outfit : {};\n const ranks = catalogue.slotOrder.map((slot) => (\n catalogue.rarityOrder.indexOf(itemRarity(slot, source[slot], catalogue))\n ));\n return catalogue.rarityOrder[Math.max(0, ...ranks)];\n}\n\n/**\n * @description Says whether an outfit has a legendary item, which earns the sparkle aura and a\n * commentary line (SPEC.md § 9).\n * @param {Object} outfit - An outfit.\n * @param {Object} [catalogue] - The theme's outfits section.\n * @returns {boolean} True when any item is of the rarest tier.\n * @example\n * isLegendary({fur: 'rainbow'});\n * // true\n * @since 1.0.0\n */\nexport function isLegendary(outfit, catalogue = themeConfig.outfits) {\n const rarest = catalogue.rarityOrder[catalogue.rarityOrder.length - 1];\n return outfitRarity(outfit, catalogue) === rarest;\n}\n\n/**\n * @description Makes the outfit sent to POST /draw: only the four allowed keys, and only values\n * that match the server's id rule, so the draw never fails with bad_outfit. A value that does\n * not match is left out, and the server stores what remains.\n * @param {*} outfit - Any value.\n * @returns {{hat?: string, cape?: string, accessory?: string, fur?: string}} The payload outfit.\n * @example\n * toPayload({hat: 'viking', cape: '<script>', extra: 'x'});\n * // {hat: 'viking'}\n * @since 1.0.0\n */\nexport function toPayload(outfit) {\n const source = outfit && typeof outfit === 'object' ? outfit : {};\n const payload = {};\n PAYLOAD_SLOTS.forEach((slot) => {\n const value = Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(source, slot) ? source[slot] : undefined;\n if (typeof value === 'string' && OUTFIT_ID_PATTERN.test(value)) {\n payload[slot] = value;\n }\n });\n return payload;\n}\n\n/**\n * @description Fills an outfit for drawing: a missing slot or an id this catalogue does not know\n * (say, from an older theme) becomes the slot's default, so a stored {} draws a plain squirrel.\n * @param {*} outfit - A stored or rolled outfit.\n * @param {Object} [catalogue] - The theme's outfits section.\n * @returns {{hat: string, cape: string, accessory: string, fur: string}} A drawable outfit.\n * @example\n * outfitForDrawing({});\n * // {hat: 'none', cape: 'none', accessory: 'none', fur: 'red'}\n * @since 1.0.0\n */\nexport function outfitForDrawing(outfit, catalogue = themeConfig.outfits) {\n const source = outfit && typeof outfit === 'object' ? outfit : {};\n const drawable = {};\n catalogue.slotOrder.forEach((slot) => {\n const known = findItem(slot, source[slot], catalogue);\n drawable[slot] = known ? known.id : catalogue.defaults[slot];\n });\n return drawable;\n}\n","/**\n * Thin client for the Squirrel Race REST API at /api/x_crli_squirrel/race (SPEC.md § 7).\n *\n * Every call goes through aiuxFetch, which adds the session's XSRF and auth headers, with a\n * relative URL so the AIUX request handling can do its job. The server is the real gate: it\n * checks the marshal role and answers 403, which arrives here as a RaceApiError with code\n * 'forbidden' so the page can say \"Marshals only\".\n *\n * Responses are read tolerantly: a body wrapped in {result: ...} (what a scripted REST\n * resource's setBody() produces) or a bare body both work, and the shared error shape\n * {error: {code, message, details}} or the platform's own {error: {message, detail}} both turn\n * into a RaceApiError with status, code and details.\n *\n * This module is the only one in lib/ that imports from the platform, so it is not unit tested\n * under Node; the M3 and M5 checks cover it through the browser.\n */\nimport {aiuxFetch} from '@servicenow/aiux/aiux-components-core';\nimport {toPayload} from './outfits.js';\n\nconst BASE_PATH = '/api/x_crli_squirrel/race';\nconst SYS_ID_PATTERN = /^[0-9a-f]{32}$/;\nconst DEFAULT_LIMIT = 10;\nconst MAX_LIMIT = 25;\nconst GROUP_QUERY_MIN_LENGTH = 2;\n// Codes for statuses that arrive without the shared error shape (a platform 401, for example).\nconst STATUS_CODES = {401: 'unauthenticated', 403: 'forbidden', 404: 'not_found'};\n\n/**\n * A failed call to the race API, carrying the HTTP status, the error code (SPEC.md § 7: no_names,\n * too_many, name_too_long, duplicate_names, bad_places, bad_mode, bad_length, bad_outfit,\n * not_found, forbidden, draw_failed; plus network_error, unauthenticated and http_error from\n * this client) and the details (for example the offending names).\n */\nexport class RaceApiError extends Error {\n /**\n * @description Builds the error.\n * @param {string} message - A readable message.\n * @param {{status?: number, code?: string, details?: string[]}} [parts] - Status (0 when the\n * server was not reached), code and details.\n * @since 1.0.0\n */\n constructor(message, {status = 0, code = 'http_error', details = []} = {}) {\n super(message);\n this.name = 'RaceApiError';\n this.status = status;\n this.code = code;\n this.details = Array.isArray(details) ? details.map(String) : [];\n }\n}\n\n/**\n * @description Unwraps a {result: ...} body, or returns the body as it is.\n * @param {*} body - The parsed body.\n * @returns {*} The payload.\n * @since 1.0.0\n */\nfunction unwrapResult(body) {\n const wrapped = body && typeof body === 'object' && !Array.isArray(body)\n && Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(body, 'result');\n return wrapped ? body.result : body;\n}\n\n/**\n * @description Reads a response body as JSON, or null when there is none or it is not JSON.\n * @param {Object} response - The aiuxFetch response.\n * @returns {Promise<*>} The parsed body, or null.\n * @since 1.0.0\n */\nasync function readBody(response) {\n try {\n return await response.json();\n } catch {\n return null;\n }\n}\n\n/**\n * @description Turns a failed response into a RaceApiError. On the\\n * server it does nothing, so a stray call during server rendering is harmless.\\n */\\nimport {isServer} from 'lit';\\nimport {i18n} from '@servicenow/aiux/aiux-services';\\n\\n/**\\n * @description Sets the browser tab title to \\\"<page> | Squirrel Scramble\\\", or to the app name\\n *   alone when no page title is given.\\n * @param {string} pageTitle - The page's own title, already translated.\\n * @returns {void}\\n * @example\\n *   setDocumentTitle(i18n.getMessage('Hall of Fame'));\\n *   // document.title === 'Hall of Fame | Squirrel Scramble'\\n * @since 1.0.0\\n */\\nexport function setDocumentTitle(pageTitle) {\\n  if (isServer || typeof document === 'undefined') {\\n    return;\\n  }\\n  const cleaned = typeof pageTitle === 'string' ? pageTitle.trim() : '';\\n  document.title = cleaned\\n    ? i18n.getMessage('{page} | Squirrel Scramble', {page: cleaned})\\n    : i18n.getMessage('Squirrel Scramble');\\n}\\n\",\"/**\\n * App-relative routes for the Squirrel Scramble experience, all under one version segment.\\n *\\n * Why the version: the Lux cloud service caches each experience's route list and each page's\\n * bundle, and doesn't refresh either after a redeploy (SPEC.md § 23, decision 9). Only a route\\n * path, a custom-element tag and a basename it has never seen get a changed page served. So every\\n * app route starts with ROUTE_VERSION, and the pages and application.js build their paths here\\n * instead of writing them out.\\n *\\n * A redeploy that changes a page:\\n *   1. Bump ROUTE_VERSION (for example 'v7' to 'v8').\\n *   2. Move every page folder to match: pages/<old>/<route>/ becomes pages/<new>/<route>/.\\n *      File-based routing reads the folder names and can't read this constant, so the two must\\n *      agree by hand. The folders stay at the same depth, so their relative imports don't change.\\n *      Leave pages/race/ where it is: /race is the redirect for the cached M0 shell's sidebar\\n *      \\\"Race\\\" link, so its path never changes, and it reaches the new version through\\n *      playRoute() by itself.\\n *   3. Rename every page's @customElement tag to the new version\\n *      (x-crli-squirrel-<page>-<new>-page), so the build makes new widget records. That includes\\n *      the /race redirect: x-crli-squirrel-race-redirect-<old>-page becomes\\n *      x-crli-squirrel-race-redirect-<new>-page, although its folder stays put.\\n *   4. Change the basename in aiux.json, and set its landing to the new routeFor('play').\\n *   5. Re-point every platform record that holds a Lux path at the new URLs:\\n *      - the four DIRECT sys_app_module rows in the \\\"Squirrel Scramble\\\" application menu, each\\n *        with its query set to /aiux/scramble-vN/vN/<page>:\\n *          \\\"Start a race\\\" (/vN/play),\\n *          \\\"Race history screen\\\" (/vN/history),\\n *          \\\"Hall of Fame\\\" (/vN/hall-of-fame),\\n *          \\\"Wardrobe\\\" (/vN/wardrobe);\\n *      - the \\\"Replay\\\" UI action on the Race table: the SQUIRREL_REPLAY_BASE line in its script,\\n *        and its comments.\\n *      The last three links exist because Lux kept serving a cached older app shell whose\\n *      side-nav links point at an old route version (Chaos v2 contract § 13; SPEC.md § 23,\\n *      decision 9), so the platform menu carries direct links until Lux refreshes the shell.\\n *      Since 2026-11-05 the pages also repair that shell themselves: each page's firstUpdated()\\n *      calls repairStaleShell() (utils/shell.js), which resets the nav items to this version's\\n *      routes and hides the chat bar. The direct menu links stay as a second way in.\\n *\\n * 2026-11-05: v6 became v7 although no page changed its behaviour after the v6 deploy. Lux kept\\n * serving the 11:40 v6 page bundles (the 13:31 v6 build's new files returned 404), so the shell\\n * repair above never reached the browser under v6. v7 ships it under a route, tags and a\\n * basename Lux has not seen.\\n *\\n * REST paths (/api/x_crli_squirrel/...) are not app routes and don't belong here.\\n */\\n\\n/** The version segment every app route starts with. Bump it on a redeploy that changes a page. */\\nexport const ROUTE_VERSION = 'v7';\\n\\n/** The pages routeFor() knows, by their folder name under pages/<ROUTE_VERSION>/. */\\nconst PAGE_NAMES = Object.freeze(['play', 'history', 'hall-of-fame', 'wardrobe']);\\n\\n/** The start of every replay path: a replay lives at <REPLAY_ROUTE_PREFIX>/<sys_id>. */\\nexport const REPLAY_ROUTE_PREFIX = `/${ROUTE_VERSION}/replay`;\\n\\n/**\\n * @description Builds the app-relative path of a page, under the current route version.\\n * @param {string} name - The page's folder name: 'play', 'history', 'hall-of-fame' or\\n *   'wardrobe'.\\n * @returns {string} The path, for example '/v7/history' while ROUTE_VERSION is 'v7'.\\n * @throws {Error} When the name is not one of the app's pages.\\n * @example\\n *   navigate(routeFor('history'));\\n * @since 1.0.0\\n */\\nexport function routeFor(name) {\\n  if (!PAGE_NAMES.includes(name)) {\\n    throw new Error(`Squirrel Scramble has no page called '${String(name)}'.`);\\n  }\\n  return `/${ROUTE_VERSION}/${name}`;\\n}\\n\\n/**\\n * @description Builds the app-relative path of a stored race's replay page.\\n * @param {string} sysId - The race's sys_id. Callers check its shape first.\\n * @returns {string} The path, for example '/v7/replay/<sys_id>' while ROUTE_VERSION is 'v7'.\\n * @throws {Error} When sysId is not a non-empty string.\\n * @example\\n *   navigate(replayRoute(race.sysId));\\n * @since 1.0.0\\n */\\nexport function replayRoute(sysId) {\\n  if (typeof sysId !== 'string' || sysId === '') {\\n    throw new Error('A replay route needs the race sys_id.');\\n  }\\n  return `${REPLAY_ROUTE_PREFIX}/${encodeURIComponent(sysId)}`;\\n}\\n\\n/**\\n * @description Builds the app-relative path of the race page. With a rematch sys_id the setup\\n *   view opens with that race's line-up, linked as a rematch (the page's loader reads\\n *   ?rematch=).\\n * @param {{rematch?: string}} [options] - Options; rematch is the sys_id of the race to rematch,\\n *   and empty or missing gives the plain race page.\\n * @returns {string} '/v7/play' or '/v7/play?rematch=<sys_id>' while ROUTE_VERSION is 'v7'.\\n * @throws {never} Never throws.\\n * @example\\n *   navigate(playRoute({rematch: race.sysId}));\\n *   navigate(playRoute());\\n * @since 1.0.0\\n */\\nexport function playRoute(options) {\\n  const rematch = options && typeof options.rematch === 'string' ? options.rematch : '';\\n  const path = routeFor('play');\\n  return rematch ? `${path}?rematch=${encodeURIComponent(rematch)}` : path;\\n}\\n\",\"/**\\n * The Squirrel Scramble shell, as plain data: the four nav items, the shell features, the whole\\n * navLayoutContext value, and the app route read from a browser path. The one place the nav list\\n * is written: application.js setup() and the pages' repair (utils/shell.js) both build from here.\\n *\\n * The module has no platform imports on purpose: the i18n service is passed in, so the Node tests\\n * can run it with a stub, and the build still sees literal i18n.getMessage() calls (the i18n lint\\n * rule getmessage-no-variable-arg and the string extractor accept only a literal argument, as in\\n * components/audio/sound-labels.js). Paths come from utils/routes.js, which has no imports either.\\n */\\nimport {REPLAY_ROUTE_PREFIX, routeFor} from './routes.js';\\n\\n/**\\n * Routes that belong to a nav item without being its own path: a replay is opened from the\\n * History page, so History stays highlighted while it plays.\\n */\\nconst ACTIVE_PREFIXES = Object.freeze({\\n  [routeFor('history')]: Object.freeze([REPLAY_ROUTE_PREFIX])\\n});\\n\\n/**\\n * The shell features (Chaos v2 contract § 13). Two are off for the race: chat, so the shell's\\n * \\\"Ask or search for anything\\\" bar never shows, and onboarding, so the \\\"Get to know Lux\\\" popup\\n * never covers the stage.\\n */\\nexport const SHELL_FEATURES = Object.freeze({\\n  menus: false,\\n  logo: true,\\n  userSession: false,\\n  notifications: false,\\n  themeToggle: false,\\n  densityPicker: false,\\n  unifiedExperience: false,\\n  profile: true,\\n  helpPanel: true,\\n  chat: false,\\n  onboarding: false\\n});\\n\\n/**\\n * The event the nav layout's ChatController listens for on its host\\n * (handleChatVisibilityChange): detail.hidden true hides the chat bar for the page.\\n */\\nexport const CHAT_VISIBILITY_EVENT = 'aiux-chat-visibility-change';\\n\\n/** The Lux URL prefix: /aiux/<basename>, the basename being aiux.json's. */\\nconst AIUX_PREFIX = /^\\\\/aiux\\\\/[^/]+(?=\\\\/|$)/;\\n\\n/**\\n * @description Says whether a nav item should show as the current page.\\n * @param {{action?: {path?: string}}} item - The nav item.\\n * @param {string} activePath - The active app route: routeFor('play'), say, or a replay's\\n *   REPLAY_ROUTE_PREFIX followed by '/<sys_id>' (or the route pattern's '/:id').\\n * @returns {boolean} True when the item's path or one of its extra prefixes matches.\\n * @throws {never} Never throws.\\n * @example\\n *   isItemActive({action: {path: '/v7/history'}}, '/v7/replay/abc'); // true\\n * @since 1.0.0\\n */\\nexport function isItemActive(item, activePath) {\\n  const itemPath = item && item.action ? item.action.path : '';\\n  if (!itemPath || typeof activePath !== 'string' || !activePath) {\\n    return false;\\n  }\\n  if (activePath === itemPath) {\\n    return true;\\n  }\\n  const prefixes = ACTIVE_PREFIXES[itemPath] || [];\\n  return prefixes.some((prefix) => activePath.startsWith(prefix));\\n}\\n\\n/**\\n * @description Builds the four nav items (Race, History, Hall of Fame, Wardrobe) under the\\n *   current route version, with the current page's item marked active. Icon names are native\\n *   Horizon icons from the installed @servicenow/aiux icon list.\\n * @param {{getMessage: function(string, ...*): string}} i18n - The AIUX i18n service, or a stub.\\n * @param {string} activePath - The active app route, for example '/v7/wardrobe'; empty marks\\n *   nothing.\\n * @returns {Array<Object>} New item objects; only the active one carries active: true.\\n * @throws {never} Never throws for a service whose getMessage doesn't.\\n * @example\\n *   createNavItems(i18n, '/v7/replay/abc').find((item) => item.active).icon; // 'history'\\n * @since 1.0.0\\n */\\nexport function createNavItems(i18n, activePath) {\\n  const items = [\\n    {\\n      icon: 'flag-event',\\n      title: i18n.getMessage('Race'),\\n      action: {type: 'navigate', path: routeFor('play')}\\n    },\\n    {\\n      icon: 'history',\\n      title: i18n.getMessage('History'),\\n      action: {type: 'navigate', path: routeFor('history')}\\n    },\\n    {\\n      icon: 'star',\\n      title: i18n.getMessage('Hall of Fame'),\\n      action: {type: 'navigate', path: routeFor('hall-of-fame')}\\n    },\\n    {\\n      icon: 'palette',\\n      title: i18n.getMessage('Wardrobe'),\\n      action: {type: 'navigate', path: routeFor('wardrobe')}\\n    }\\n  ];\\n  return items.map((item) => (isItemActive(item, activePath) ? {...item, active: true} : item));\\n}\\n\\n/**\\n * @description Builds the whole navLayoutContext value: the current value kept, with the app\\n *   title, the shell features, the nav items and the logos set over it.\\n * @param {Object|null|undefined} current - navLayoutContext.get(), or nothing.\\n * @param {{getMessage: function(string, ...*): string}} i18n - The AIUX i18n service, or a stub.\\n * @param {string} activePath - The active app route; see createNavItems().\\n * @returns {Object} The new value to set.\\n * @throws {never} Never throws for a service whose getMessage doesn't.\\n * @example\\n *   navLayoutContext.set(buildShellState(navLayoutContext.get(), i18n, '/v7/play'));\\n * @since 1.0.0\\n */\\nexport function buildShellState(current, i18n, activePath) {\\n  const base = current && typeof current === 'object' ? current : {};\\n  return {\\n    ...base,\\n    appTitle: i18n.getMessage('Squirrel Scramble'),\\n    features: {...SHELL_FEATURES},\\n    items: createNavItems(i18n, activePath),\\n    defaultLogoFull: 'servicenow',\\n    defaultLogoIcon: 'servicenow'\\n  };\\n}\\n\\n/**\\n * @description Reads the app route from a browser path: drops the /aiux/<basename> prefix and\\n *   any trailing slash. A path without the prefix (a local dev server) is taken as it is.\\n * @param {string} pathname - location.pathname, for example\\n *   '/aiux/scramble-v7/v7/hall-of-fame'.\\n * @returns {string} The app route, for example '/v7/hall-of-fame'; '/' for the app root; '' when\\n *   the input is not a non-empty string.\\n * @throws {never} Never throws.\\n * @example\\n *   routePathFromPathname('/aiux/scramble-v7/v7/replay/abc/'); // '/v7/replay/abc'\\n * @since 1.0.0\\n */\\nexport function routePathFromPathname(pathname) {\\n  if (typeof pathname !== 'string' || pathname === '') {\\n    return '';\\n  }\\n  const appPath = pathname.replace(AIUX_PREFIX, '').replace(/\\\\/+$/, '');\\n  if (appPath === '') {\\n    return '/';\\n  }\\n  return appPath.startsWith('/') ? appPath : `/${appPath}`;\\n}\\n\",\"/**\\n * The Squirrel Scramble shell, wired to the platform: sets navLayoutContext from the one nav\\n * builder (utils/shell-nav.js), and lets a page repair a stale shell.\\n *\\n * Why the repair: the Lux rendering service kept serving a cached older application.js (the v5\\n * shell), whose nav items point at /v5/ routes that no longer exist and which lacks\\n * features.chat: false (Chaos v2 contract § 13; SPEC.md § 23, decision 9). So every v7 page\\n * calls repairStaleShell(this) from firstUpdated(): it sets the current nav items and features,\\n * and asks the nav layout to hide the chat bar. With a fresh shell it changes nothing that shows.\\n *\\n * Client only for the repair: pages call it from firstUpdated(), never from render() or the\\n * constructor. On the server it does nothing.\\n */\\nimport {isServer} from 'lit';\\nimport {navLayoutContext} from '@servicenow/aiux/aiux-components-nav';\\nimport {i18n} from '@servicenow/aiux/aiux-services';\\nimport {\\n  CHAT_VISIBILITY_EVENT,\\n  buildShellState,\\n  createNavItems,\\n  routePathFromPathname\\n} from './shell-nav.js';\\n\\n/**\\n * @description Builds the four nav items in the current language, with the active page marked\\n *   (a replay marks History).\\n * @param {string} activePath - The active app route, for example '/v7/wardrobe'.\\n * @returns {Array<Object>} The nav items.\\n * @throws {never} Never throws.\\n * @example\\n *   buildNavItems(routeFor('history'));\\n * @since 1.0.0\\n */\\nexport function buildNavItems(activePath) {\\n  return createNavItems(i18n, activePath);\\n}\\n\\n/**\\n * @description Sets navLayoutContext: the app title, the shell features (chat and onboarding\\n *   off) and the nav items, over whatever the context already holds.\\n * @param {string} activePath - The active app route, for example '/v7/play'.\\n * @returns {boolean} True when the context was set; false when there is no context to set.\\n * @throws {Error} Whatever navLayoutContext.set() throws; repairStaleShell() catches it.\\n * @example\\n *   applyShellNav(routeFor('play'));\\n * @since 1.0.0\\n */\\nexport function applyShellNav(activePath) {\\n  const context = navLayoutContext;\\n  if (!context || typeof context.get !== 'function' || typeof context.set !== 'function') {\\n    return false;\\n  }\\n  context.set(buildShellState(context.get(), i18n, activePath));\\n  return true;\\n}\\n\\n/**\\n * @description Reads the current app route from the browser address.\\n * @returns {string} The app route, for example '/v7/history'; '' when there is no location.\\n * @throws {never} Never throws.\\n * @example\\n *   currentRoutePath(); // '/v7/history' at /aiux/scramble-v7/v7/history\\n * @since 1.0.0\\n */\\nfunction currentRoutePath() {\\n  if (typeof window === 'undefined' || !window.location) {\\n    return '';\\n  }\\n  return routePathFromPathname(window.location.pathname);\\n}\\n\\n/**\\n * @description Repairs a stale cached shell from the page: sets the current nav items and\\n *   features for the current route, then dispatches the chat-visibility event from the page so\\n *   the nav layout hides the chat bar. Client only (a no-op on the server), and never throws: a\\n *   missing context or host is skipped, and each step's failure is swallowed so the page still\\n *   works.\\n * @param {HTMLElement} hostElement - The page element; the event bubbles out of its shadow root\\n *   to the nav layout.\\n * @returns {void}\\n * @throws {never} Never throws.\\n * @example\\n *   firstUpdated() {\\n *     repairStaleShell(this);\\n *   }\\n * @since 1.0.0\\n */\\nexport function repairStaleShell(hostElement) {\\n  if (isServer || typeof window === 'undefined') {\\n    return;\\n  }\\n  try {\\n    applyShellNav(currentRoutePath());\\n  } catch {\\n    // The nav repair is cosmetic: the page works without it.\\n  }\\n  try {\\n    if (hostElement && typeof hostElement.dispatchEvent ===   composed: true\\n      }));\\n    }\\n  } catch {\\n    // Hiding the chat bar is cosmetic too.\\n  }\\n}\\n\"],\"names\":[\"setDocumentTitle\",\"pageTitle\",\"isServer\",\"document\",\"cleaned\",\"trim\",\"title\",\"i18n\",\"getMessage\",\"page\",\"PAGE_NAMES\",\"Object\",\"freeze\",\"REPLAY_ROUTE_PREFIX\",\"routeFor\",\"name\",\"includes\",\"Error\",\"String\",\"replayRoute\",\"sysId\",\"encodeURIComponent\",\"playRoute\",\"options\",\"rematch\",\"path\",\"ACTIVE_PREFIXES\",\"SHELL_FEATURES\",\"menus\",\"logo\",\"userSession\",\"notifications\",\"themeToggle\",\"densityPicker\",\"unifiedExperience\",\"profile\",\"helpPanel\",\"chat\",\"onboarding\",\"AIUX_PREFIX\",\"repairStaleShell\",\"hostElement\",\"window\",\"applyShellNav\",\"activePath\",\"current\",\"navLayoutContext\",\"context\",\"get\",\"set\",\"appTitle\",\"features\",\"items\",\"icon\",\"action\",\"type\",\"map\",\"item\",\"itemPath\",\"isItemActive\",\"prefixes\",\"some\",\"prefix\",\"startsWith\",\"active\",\"defaultLogoFull\",\"defaultLogoIcon\",\"currentRoutePath\",\"location\",\"pathname\",\"appPath\",\"replace\",\"dispatchEvent\",\"CustomEvent\",\"detail\",\"hidden\",\"bubbles\",\"composed\"],\"mappings\":\"4IAmBO,SAASA,EAAiBC,CAAS,EACxC,GAAIC,GAAY,AAAoB,IAApB,OAAOC,SACrB,OAEF,IAAMC,EAAU,AAAqB,UAArB,OAAOH,EAAyBA,EAAUI,IAAI,GAAK,EACnEF,CAAAA,SAASG,KAAK,CAAGF,EACbG,EAAKC,UAAU,CAAC,6BAA8B,CAACC,KAAML,IACrDG,EAAKC,UAAU,CAAC,oBACtB,CCuBA,IAAME,EAAaC,OAAOC,MAAM,CAAC,CAAC,OAAQ,UAAW,eAAgB,WAAW,EAGnEC,EAAsB,aAY5B,SAASC,EAASC,CAAI,EAC3B,GAAI,CAACL,EAAWM,QAAQ,CAACD,GACvB,MAAM,AAAIE,MAAM,CAAC,sCAAsC,EAAEC,OAAOH,GAAM,EAAE,CAAC,EAE3E,MAAO,OAAqBA,GAAM,AACpC,CAWO,SAASI,EAAYC,CAAK,EAC/B,GAAI,AAAiB,UAAjB,OAAOA,GAAsBA,AAAU,KAAVA,EAC/B,MAAM,AAAIH,MAAM,yCAElB,MAAO,CAAA,EAAGJ,EAAoB,CAAC,EAAEQ,mBAAmBD,GAAAA,CAAQ,AAC9D,CAeO,SAASE,EAAUC,CAAO,EAC/B,IAAMC,EAAUD,GAAW,AAA2B,UAA3B,OAAOA,EAAQC,OAAO,CAAgBD,EAAQC,OAAO,CAAG,GAC7EC,EAAOX,EAAS,QACtB,OAAOU,EAAU,CAAA,EAAGC,EAAK,SAAS,EAAEJ,mBAAmBG,IAAU,CAAGC,CACtE,CCzFA,IAAMC,EAAkBf,OAAOC,MAAM,CAAC,CACpC,CAACE,EAAS,WAAA,CAAaH,OAAOC,MAAM,CAAC,CAACC,EAAoB,CAC5D,GAOac,EAAiBhB,OAAOC,MAA Scramble">6034db60bdae62650172468867a73546</source_aix_project><source_browser_code/><sourcemap>{"version":3,"file":"shell-ycxiky2b.js","sources":["../../../utils/document-title.js","../../../utils/routes.js","../../../utils/shell-nav.js","../../../utils/shell.js"],"sourcesContent":["/**\n * Browser tab titles for Squirrel Scramble pages (WCAG 2.2 SC 2.4.2, Page Titled).\n *\n * Client only: pages call it from firstUpdated() or an event handler, never from render(). On the\n * server it does nothing, so a stray call during server rendering is harmless.\n */\nimport {isServer} from 'lit';\nimport {i18n} from '@servicenow/aiux/aiux-services';\n\n/**\n * @description Sets the browser tab title to \"<page> | Squirrel Scramble\", or to the app name\n *   alone when no page title is given.\n * @param {string} pageTitle - The page's own title, already translated.\n * @returns {void}\n * @example\n *   setDocumentTitle(i18n.getMessage('Hall of Fame'));\n *   // document.title === 'Hall of Fame | Squirrel Scramble'\n * @since 1.0.0\n */\nexport function setDocumentTitle(pageTitle) {\n  if (isServer || typeof document === 'undefined') {\n    return;\n  }\n  const cleaned = typeof pageTitle === 'string' ? pageTitle.trim() : '';\n  document.title = cleaned\n    ? i18n.getMessage('{page} | Squirrel Scramble', {page: cleaned})\n    : i18n.getMessage('Squirrel Scramble');\n}\n","/**\n * App-relative routes for the Squirrel Scramble experience, all under one version segment.\n *\n * Why the version: the Lux cloud service caches each experience's route list and each page's\n * bundle, and doesn't refresh either after a redeploy (SPEC.md § 23, decision 9). Only a route\n * path, a custom-element tag and a basename it has never seen get a changed page served. So every\n * app route starts with ROUTE_VERSION, and the pages and application.js build their paths here\n * instead of writing them out.\n *\n * A redeploy that changes a page:\n *   1. Bump ROUTE_VERSION (for example 'v7' to 'v8').\n *   2. Move every page folder to match: pages/<old>/<route>/ becomes pages/<new>/<route>/.\n *      File-based routing reads the folder names and can't read this constant, so the two must\n *      agree by hand. The folders stay at the same depth, so their relative imports don't change.\n *      Leave pages/race/ where it is: /race is the redirect for the cached M0 shell's sidebar\n *      \"Race\" link, so its path never changes, and it reaches the new version through\n *      playRoute() by itself.\n *   3. Rename every page's @customElement tag to the new version\n *      (x-crli-squirrel-<page>-<new>-page), so the build makes new widget records. That includes\n *      the /race redirect: x-crli-squirrel-race-redirect-<old>-page becomes\n *      x-crli-squirrel-race-redirect-<new>-page, although its folder stays put.\n *   4. Change the basename in aiux.json, and set its landing to the new routeFor('play').\n *   5. Re-point every platform record that holds a Lux path at the new URLs:\n *      - the four DIRECT sys_app_module rows in the \"Squirrel Scramble\" application menu, each\n *        with its query set to /aiux/scramble-vN/vN/<page>:\n *          \"Start a race\" (/vN/play),\n *          \"Race history screen\" (/vN/history),\n *          \"Hall of Fame\" (/vN/hall-of-fame),\n *          \"Wardrobe\" (/vN/wardrobe);\n *      - the \"Replay\" UI action on the Race table: the SQUIRREL_REPLAY_BASE line in its script,\n *        and its comments.\n *      The last three links exist because Lux kept serving a cached older app shell whose\n *      side-nav links point at an old route version (Chaos v2 contract § 13; SPEC.md § 23,\n *      decision 9), so the platform menu carries direct links until Lux refreshes the shell.\n *      Since 2026-11-05 the pages also repair that shell themselves: each page's firstUpdated()\n *      calls repairStaleShell() (utils/shell.js), which resets the nav items to this version's\n *      routes and hides the chat bar. The direct menu links stay as a second way in.\n *\n * 2026-11-05: v6 became v7 although no page changed its behaviour after the v6 deploy. Lux kept\n * serving the 11:40 v6 page bundles (the 13:31 v6 build's new files returned 404), so the shell\n * repair above never reached the browser under v6. v7 ships it under a route, tags and a\n * basename Lux has not seen.\n *\n * REST paths (/api/x_crli_squirrel/...) are not app routes and don't belong here.\n */\n\n/** The version segment every app route starts with. Bump it on a redeploy that changes a page. */\nexport const ROUTE_VERSION = 'v7';\n\n/** The pages routeFor() knows, by their folder name under pages/<ROUTE_VERSION>/. */\nconst PAGE_NAMES = Object.freeze(['play', 'history', 'hall-of-fame', 'wardrobe']);\n\n/** The start of every replay path: a replay lives at <REPLAY_ROUTE_PREFIX>/<sys_id>. */\nexport const REPLAY_ROUTE_PREFIX = `/${ROUTE_VERSION}/replay`;\n\n/**\n * @description Builds the app-relative path of a page, under the current route version.\n * @param {string} name - The page's folder name: 'play', 'history', 'hall-of-fame' or\n *   'wardrobe'.\n * @returns {string} The path, for example '/v7/history' while ROUTE_VERSION is 'v7'.\n * @throws {Error} When the name is not one of the app's pages.\n * @example\n *   navigate(routeFor('history'));\n * @since 1.0.0\n */\nexport function routeFor(name) {\n  if (!PAGE_NAMES.includes(name)) {\n    throw new Error(`Squirrel Scramble has no page called '${String(name)}'.`);\n  }\n  return `/${ROUTE_VERSION}/${name}`;\n}\n\n/**\n * @description Builds the app-relative path of a stored race's replay page.\n * @param {string} sysId - The race's sys_id. Callers check its shape first.\n * @returns {string} The path, for example '/v7/replay/<sys_id>' while ROUTE_VERSION is 'v7'.\n * @throws {Error} When sysId is not a non-empty string.\n * @example\n *   navigate(replayRoute(race.sysId));\n * @since 1.0.0\n */\nexport function replayRoute(sysId) {\n  if (typeof sysId !== 'string' || sysId === '') {\n    throw new Error('A replay route needs the race sys_id.');\n  }\n  return `${REPLAY_ROUTE_PREFIX}/${encodeURIComponent(sysId)}`;\n}\n\n/**\n * @description Builds the app-relative path of the race page. With a rematch sys_id the setup\n *   view opens with that race's line-up, linked as a rematch (the page's loader reads\n *   ?rematch=).\n * @param {{rematch?: string}} [options] - Options; rematch is the sys_id of the race to rematch,\n *   and empty or missing gives the plain race page.\n * @returns {string} '/v7/play' or '/v7/play?rematch=<sys_id>' while ROUTE_VERSION is 'v7'.\n * @throws {never} Never throws.\n * @example\n *   navigate(playRoute({rematch: race.sysId}));\n *   navigate(playRoute());\n * @since 1.0.0\n */\nexport function playRoute(options) {\n  const rematch = options && typeof options.rematch === 'string' ? options.rematch : '';\n  const path = routeFor('play');\n  return rematch ? `${path}?rematch=${encodeURIComponent(rematch)}` : path;\n}\n","/**\n * The Squirrel Scramble shell, as plain data: the four nav items, the shell features, the whole\n * navLayoutContext value, and the app route read from a browser path. The one place the nav list\n * is written: application.js setup() and the pages' repair (utils/shell.js) both build from here.\n *\n * The module has no platform imports on purpose: the i18n service is passed in, so the Node tests\n * can run it with a stub, and the build still sees literal i18n.getMessage() calls (the i18n lint\n * rule getmessage-no-variable-arg and the string extractor accept only a literal argument, as in\n * components/audio/sound-labels.js). Paths come from utils/routes.js, which has no imports either.\n */\nimport {REPLAY_ROUTE_PREFIX, routeFor} from './routes.js';\n\n/**\n * Routes that belong to a nav item without being its own path: a replay is opened from the\n * History page, so History stays highlighted while it plays.\n */\nconst ACTIVE_PREFIXES = Object.freeze({\n  [routeFor('history')]: Object.freeze([REPLAY_ROUTE_PREFIX])\n});\n\n/**\n * The shell features (Chaos v2 contract § 13). Two are off for the race: chat, so the shell's\n * \"Ask or search for anything\" bar never shows, and onboarding, so the \"Get to know Lux\" popup\n * never covers the stage.\n */\nexport const SHELL_FEATURES = Object.freeze({\n  menus: false,\n  logo: true,\n  userSession: false,\n  notifications: false,\n  themeToggle: false,\n  densityPicker: false,\n  unifiedExperience: false,\n  profile: true,\n  helpPanel: true,\n  chat: false,\n  onboarding: false\n});\n\n/**\n * The event the nav layout's ChatController listens for on its host\n * (handleChatVisibilityChange): detail.hidden true hides the chat bar for the page.\n */\nexport const CHAT_VISIBILITY_EVENT = 'aiux-chat-visibility-change';\n\n/** The Lux URL prefix: /aiux/<basename>, the basename being aiux.json's. */\nconst AIUX_PREFIX = /^\\/aiux\\/[^/]+(?=\\/|$)/;\n\n/**\n * @description Says whether a nav item should show as the current page.\n * @param {{action?: {path?: string}}} item - The nav item.\n * @param {string} activePath - The active app route: routeFor('play'), say, or a replay's\n *   REPLAY_ROUTE_PREFIX followed by '/<sys_id>' (or the route pattern's '/:id').\n * @returns {boolean} True when the item's path or one of its extra prefixes matches.\n * @throws {never} Never throws.\n * @example\n *   isItemActive({action: {path: '/v7/history'}}, '/v7/replay/abc'); // true\n * @since 1.0.0\n */\nexport function isItemActive(item, activePath) {\n  const itemPath = item && item.action ? item.action.path : '';\n  if (!itemPath || typeof activePath !== 'string' || !activePath) {\n    return false;\n  }\n  if (activePath === itemPath) {\n    return true;\n  }\n  const prefixes = ACTIVE_PREFIXES[itemPath] || [];\n  return prefixes.some((prefix) => activePath.startsWith(prefix));\n}\n\n/**\n * @description Builds the four nav items (Race, History, Hall of Fame, Wardrobe) under the\n *   current route version, with the current page's item marked active. Icon names are native\n *   Horizon icons from the installed @servicenow/aiux icon list.\n * @param {{getMessage: function(string, ...*): string}} i18n - The AIUX i18n service, or a stub.\n * @param {string} activePath - The active app route, for example '/v7/wardrobe'; empty marks\n *   nothing.\n * @returns {Array<Object>} New item objects; only the active one carries active: true.\n * @throws {never} Never throws for a service whose getMessage doesn't.\n * @example\n *   createNavItems(i18n, '/v7/replay/abc').find((item) => item.active).icon; // 'history'\n * @since 1.0.0\n */\nexport function createNavItems(i18n, activePath) {\n  const items = [\n    {\n      icon: 'flag-event',\n      title: i18n.getMessage('Race'),\n      action: {type: 'navigate', path: routeFor('play')}\n    },\n    {\n      icon: 'history',\n      title: i18n.getMessage('History'),\n      action: {type: 'navigate', path: routeFor('history')}\n    },\n    {\n      icon: 'star',\n      title: i18n.getMessage('Hall of Fame'),\n      action: {type: 'navigate', path: routeFor('hall-of-fame')}\n    },\n    {\n      icon: 'palette',\n      title: i18n.getMessage('Wardrobe'),\n      action: {type: 'navigate', path: routeFor('wardrobe')}\n    }\n  ];\n  return items.map((item) => (isItemActive(item, activePath) ? {...item, active: true} : item));\n}\n\n/**\n * @description Builds the whole navLayoutContext value: the current value kept, with the app\n *   title, the shell features, the nav items and the logos set over it.\n * @param {Object|null|undefined} current - navLayoutContext.get(), or nothing.\n * @param {{getMessage: function(string, ...*): string}} i18n - The AIUX i18n service, or a stub.\n * @param {string} activePath - The active app route; see createNavItems().\n * @returns {Object} The new value to set.\n * @throws {never} Never throws for a service whose getMessage doesn't.\n * @example\n *   navLayoutContext.set(buildShellState(navLayoutContext.get(), i18n, '/v7/play'));\n * @since 1.0.0\n */\nexport function buildShellState(current, i18n, activePath) {\n  const base = current && typeof current === 'object' ? current : {};\n  return {\n    ...base,\n    appTitle: i18n.getMessage('Squirrel Scramble'),\n    features: {...SHELL_FEATURES},\n    items: createNavItems(i18n, activePath),\n    defaultLogoFull: 'servicenow',\n    defaultLogoIcon: 'servicenow'\n  };\n}\n\n/**\n * @description Reads the app route from a browser path: drops the /aiux/<basename> prefix and\n *   any trailing slash. A path without the prefix (a local dev server) is taken as it is.\n * @param {string} pathname - location.pathname, for example\n *   '/aiux/scramble-v7/v7/hall-of-fame'.\n * @returns {string} The app route, for example '/v7/hall-of-fame'; '/' for the app root; '' when\n *   the input is not a non-empty string.\n * @throws {never} Never throws.\n * @example\n *   routePathFromPathname('/aiux/scramble-v7/v7/replay/abc/'); // '/v7/replay/abc'\n * @since 1.0.0\n */\nexport function routePathFromPathname(pathname) {\n  if (typeof pathname !== 'string' || pathname === '') {\n    return '';\n  }\n  const appPath = pathname.replace(AIUX_PREFIX, '').replace(/\\/+$/, '');\n  if (appPath === '') {\n    return '/';\n  }\n  return appPath.startsWith('/') ? appPath : `/${appPath}`;\n}\n","/**\n * The Squirrel Scramble shell, wired to the platform: sets navLayoutContext from the one nav\n * builder (utils/shell-nav.js), and lets a page repair a stale shell.\n *\n * Why the repair: the Lux rendering service kept serving a cached older application.js (the v5\n * shell), whose nav items point at /v5/ routes that no longer exist and which lacks\n * features.chat: false (Chaos v2 contract § 13; SPEC.md § 23, decision 9). So every v7 page\n * calls repairStaleShell(this) from firstUpdated(): it sets the current nav items and features,\n * and asks the nav layout to hide the chat bar. With a fresh shell it changes nothing that shows.\n *\n * Client only for the repair: pages call it from firstUpdated(), never from render() or the\n * constructor.
